rationale: Exact-main benchmark #283 (run 41802594681, commit feb955d2758166ad8c4b519903fd1318b29e7d2d) completed the full three-system matrix. It qualified 68/67/66 category pairs and 28/27/26 matched ordinary-FastAPI pairs on Linux x86-64, Linux ARM64 and macOS ARM64. The stock FastAPI HTTP/1.1 validated route has lower Rust throughput, higher p95 latency and higher server CPU per operation on all six system/loop pairs. H2/H3 results are workload-specific, and the WebSocket text-echo measurements are slower. This evidence establishes a complete measurement matrix but no broad Python ASGI performance advantage. Retain compatibility and correctness gates for the uvicorn-rs PyPI distribution. The revised Python-free Rust-native performance objective is separate and is not established by this FastAPI comparison. Exact run, system, workload, raw metrics and artifact identity are in docs/benchmark-results.md and docs/benchmark-status.md.

scope.comparison: stock FastAPI and Starlette under the uvicorn-rs PyPI distribution versus Uvicorn

scope_revision.statement: Treat the uvicorn-rs PyPI distribution, implemented by the optional uvicorn-rs-py Cargo/PyO3 adapter, as the Python ASGI compatibility server without a performance superiority claim over Uvicorn. Target server performance claims at Python-free Rust-native application composition; keep Python ASGI parity and benchmark results as compatibility and regression evidence.
scope_revision.rationale: The exact-main normal-build three-system matrix shows the bodyless HTTP/1 validated route slower on all six system/loop pairs, with higher p95 latency and server CPU per operation. Body-copy cost cannot explain a bodyless GET. The same matrix contains workload-specific H2/H3 gains and regressions, and WebSocket text-echo is slower. Those measurements do not support a broad Python ASGI performance claim. Further Python-boundary work must be justified by a correctness-preserving before/after measurement. The separate Python-free Rust-native performance objective needs its own matched evidence.
